clue.text: Constituents of great condensed drink

indicators.note: a word condensed to its bare minimum keeps only its two ends, losing everything between

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
listing the two constituents joins them with the word 'and', the theme's ampersand
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drinker eyes up the ingredients of some fine concentrated beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeezing 'great' down to its outer letters leaves G and T, and naming them as a pair spells the drink with the ampersand written out, as throughout this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: G and T is the usual shorthand for a gin and tonic, a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: The number of gnomes yielding to golf authority, veteran old women

indicators.note: something yielding to another gives up its place, so one part of a word is swapped out for a newcomer

parts.note: taken as written
NO is the standard abbreviation for number, and it sits inside the word
the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, governs golf

explanation.surface: Garden ornaments are given up to the governing body of golf, leaving some elderly ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: The NO in the middle of GNOMES makes way for R AND A, giving GRANDAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandame is an archaic word for a grandmother or any old woman, so the plural suits elderly matrons.

clue.text: Biting the waitress in an old tea shop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharp and chilly, as of a wind

definitions.text: the waitress in an old tea shop
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nickname for a waitress at J. Lyons tea shops

explanation.surface: A grumpy waitress in a vintage café snaps at the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyons Corner Houses and tea shops were a British chain; their quick-footed waitresses were known as Nippies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy describes cold, biting weather, and was also the name for a Lyons tea-shop waitress.

clue.text: Naval twins with eyes on top dressing

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, so two naval men make a pair of them

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, the one written at the very start

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Identical sailors with eyes at the top of their heads, ready to put on some clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce, mayonnaise with chopped capers and gherkins, is a dressing served with fish.

clue.text: Like some doors ferry company opens for everyone so briefly

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its final letter
something that opens a thing is put inside it, splitting it open

parts.note: U, for Universal, is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages
so can mean very; trimmed of its end it becomes three letters
P and O is a well-known British ferry operator

explanation.surface: A ferry firm's cabin doors are opened for every passenger, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: P AND O sits inside U, with VERY minus its last letter tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-and-over door swings upward and back into the ceiling, as on many garages.

clue.text: University elements making Georgia the home of Museveni

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: the elements of a word here are its two ends, named one after the other as a pair

parts.note: the opening letter of the state's name
listing two elements joins them with the word 'and', the theme's ampersand
the closing letter of the state's name

explanation.surface: Parts of a university turn the American state of Georgia into an African leader's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia's outer letters G and A are named as a pair, the ampersand written as AND, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoweri Museveni has been president of Uganda since 1986, so his home country is the African state.

clue.text: See 20
A long time in the ascendancy for one playing Cupid?

indicators.note: in a down clue, something in the ascendancy rises, so the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, means for one
an actor playing a part appears as the character
Cupid is the Roman god of love

explanation.surface: Someone acting as matchmaker spends ages on top of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'for one playing Cupid' runs EG AS GOD, which is then read from the foot of the light upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's age is an informal idiom for a very long period of time.

clue.text: Museum of Sound is trash

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so the spelling follows what is heard

parts.note: lies can mean is, as in 'the answer lies here'; the ending -lise is spoken the same way

explanation.surface: A sound archive at a museum is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Museum of Sound' reads like an institution's name, but Sound applies only to the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash something is to wreck it deliberately, which is what vandalising means.

clue.text: Impressed by others, I do papers 25

indicators.note: something impressed by another is pressed into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the rest are the others
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student, awed by the people around, sits the exams a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 down, AGAIN, so the definition reads 'do papers again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination paper a second time after failing it.

clue.text: Medic keeps in a hospital post a character represented elsewhere

indicators.note: something that keeps another in holds it inside, wrapped round it
post means after, so this construction is placed after the following item

parts.note: taken as written
MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a medic
per means a, as in five pounds a head
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps someone in at the hospital, posting a character reference somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: MD holds PER and SAN, and the whole comes after A. The definition points to the theme: the & sign stands for AND in many other answers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the typographic sign &, and here the AND it stands for is written into many other lights.

clue.text: Operatic types comically run out of pianos

indicators.note: when something has run out of stock it is gone, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: grands are large concert pianos
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Singers in a comic opera tear the keyboards out of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out of' looks like a phrase, but run is a letter and 'out of' the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: G and S is Gilbert and Sullivan, whose comic operettas such as The Mikado define a type of light opera.

clue.text: GP with the case for youthful & strong support

parts.note: a GP is a family doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
the ampersand spelled out

explanation.surface: A family doctor argues the case for youth and strong backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed & is the theme symbol and is simply written out as AND. A GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry land is solid ground as opposed to water, a firm footing that bears weight.

clue.text: 25 change fitting at rear of study

indicators.note: something at the rear of another comes after it, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: An appropriate alteration is made at the back of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to AGAIN at 25 down, so the definition reads 'again change'.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to adjust or modify something once more, a second change.

clue.text: Cryptic name tag out of a drawer

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled
out of here means a letter is removed from the following group

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mysterious name label is taken out of a desk compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' wants to be a desk compartment; it is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet draws iron towards it, so it is literally a drawer, one that attracts.

clue.text: Major store my family frequents supports good food we love

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for people; read the definition as 'we who love food'

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports another sits beneath it, setting the order of the parts

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the store my family frequents is our store
M and S is Marks and Spencer, the big British retailer

explanation.surface: A family's favourite chain store stands behind the quality of food it adores.
explanation.walkthrough: M AND S plus OUR sits under G. Marks and Spencer is a British department store famous for its food hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmands are people who greatly enjoy eating, so they would describe themselves as lovers of food.

clue.text: Member representing Bude originally a long way back

parts.note: to stand for a constituency is to represent it

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a mile is a long way

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the town's name

explanation.surface: An MP sitting for the Cornish seaside town of Bude started out a long way behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' wants to be a Member of Parliament; it is a limb. Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is a limb of the body, and a forelimb is a front leg or arm.

clue.text: Broadcaster Liz taking much-needed break

indicators.note: something taking another takes it in, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: Beth, like Liz, is a short form of Elizabeth
R and R, rest and recreation, is a much-needed break

explanation.surface: A broadcaster called Liz is finally getting a well-earned holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster Liz' reads as one person; Liz is wordplay alone. Gyles Brandreth is a British TV and radio presenter and former MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyles Brandreth is a well-known British broadcaster, writer and wordplay enthusiast.

clue.text: A fill taken from Liebfraumilch, supply spirits

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb meaning in a supple, flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order
letters taken from a word are removed from it, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pours a glassful of German white wine, then provides more alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb provide, but it is the adverb from supple. Liebfraumilch is a sweet German white wine; 'spirits' wants to be alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubim are an order of angels, heavenly spirits in Christian and Jewish tradition.

clue.text: For French banker, a little facial hair trimmer

parts.note: a sou was a French coin of small value, a little money to a French banker
tache is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: A French financier trims a bit of his moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmer' wants to be a tool for the facial hair; it is a decorative trim.
explanation.definitionFit: Soutache is a narrow flat braid used as a decorative trim on clothes and upholstery.

clue.text: Name pinned to a uniform close to bird drawer

indicators.note: something pinned to another is attached directly after it, fixing the order of the pieces

parts.note: taken as written
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to dub is to name
on can mean close to, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A name tag is pinned to a uniform near a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: John James Audubon was a celebrated American naturalist who painted and drew the birds of North America.

clue.text: Model churchman has left emergency unit in pursuit of this writer

indicators.note: something that has another holds it within itself

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

indicators.note: what is in pursuit of something follows behind it, setting the order of the pieces

parts.note: the setter referring to themself
L is the abbreviation for left
A and E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital emergency department

explanation.surface: A clergyman has deserted the casualty ward to chase after a writer, who turns out to be a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, Elgar, speaking of themself; 'in pursuit of' puts the left-hand unit after that pronoun before the clergyman wraps round it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamela Anderson is a Canadian-American model and actress, famous from Playboy and Baywatch.

clue.text: Some people cut some profit

parts.note: a few means a small number of people
a bob is a short haircut

explanation.surface: A handful of people trim a bit off the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the British slang term for a shilling, so a few bob is a modest amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a few bob is a British idiom for earning a reasonable sum, a tidy profit.

clue.text: Pub enthusiast catches fish

indicators.note: something that catches another holds it, here inside itself

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub-loving angler lands a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnan, short for finnan haddie, is a smoked haddock from Scotland, a cured fish.

clue.text: Box for cigar papers in e.g. Thurber's bag

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: James Thurber was an American humorist, so his line, or bag, is humor, spelt the American way
ID papers are identity documents

explanation.surface: Someone keeps cigar papers in a bag belonging to the writer Thurber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' here is one's speciality, as in 'not my bag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A humidor is a box or case kept humid for storing cigars.

clue.text: In which the Sultan of Bow might pack up his troubles?

definitions.text: In which the Sultan of Bow might pack up his troubles?

parts.words: In which the Sultan of Bow might pack up his troubles?
parts.note: surface reading: an East End sultan stowing his worries, as in the song 'Pack Up Your Troubles in Your Old Kit Bag'; setter's reading: in Cockney rhyming slang trouble and strife means wife, so his troubles are his wives, and where a sultan keeps them is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockneys, which signals the rhyming slang: trouble and strife is wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the part of a Muslim household where a sultan's wives and concubines live.

clue.text: Outsiders dispatched nicely: as a consequence, thinly populated state

parts.note: taken as written
and can mean and so, as a consequence, as in 'he left and the party died'

explanation.surface: Eliminating outsiders politely leaves a sparsely inhabited country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic nation of fewer than 400,000 people, among Europe's least densely populated.

clue.text: Some ground made up further back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: split as ..., a gain being ground made up
second meaning: once more, returning to a former state

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning only works with the answer split into two words, a common setter's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more or back to a previous position, while a gain is ground made up in a race.

clue.text: Output from Washington perhaps stolen by errand boy?

indicators.note: something stolen by a person is tucked away on them, so the letters are concealed within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Some American government papers are pinched by a messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' wants to be the US capital; it is Dinah Washington, the 1950s singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinah Washington was a hit rhythm and blues singer, so R and B was her musical output.

clue.text: It may help to stop guest-house being considered decadent

parts.note: a B and B, bed and breakfast, is a guest-house
a rake is a dissolute, decadent man

explanation.surface: A boarding house thought of as debauched may need closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decadent' looks like an adjective but stands for a decadent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A band brake is a strap tightened round a drum to slow or halt machinery.

clue.text: Masseur initially managed to take painful private practice hit

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: something that takes another holds it inside

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
S and M, sadomasochism, is a painful practice kept private

explanation.walkthrough: S AND M goes inside RAN, after M.

clue.text: India's all out in this old one-day Cup?

definitions.note: a noun: an all-out strike in India
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a general strike in India, when everyone stays out
second meaning: the ..., Benson and Hedges Cup, a former English one-day cricket competition

explanation.walkthrough: 'All out' wants to be cricket for India's team being dismissed, which fits the cup; instead it is a strike. The Benson and Hedges Cup ran in English county cricket from 1972 to 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandh is the Hindi word for a closure or general strike, and B and H named a tobacco-sponsored cricket cup.
